subtype: Approach: tracking progress with a chart [Action]
passage: My name is Alka, and learning to skate felt slower than a snail. Some weeks I fell more than I glided. Coach Kamal said, "Mark a star on your calendar each day you practise." So I stuck one on my wall, and after every session, helmet and pads on, I drew a gold star. On bad days I still drew the star, even if I had only rolled to the gate and back. By the third week there was a row of stars like a fence. When I felt like quitting I looked at the row and thought, that is a lot of showing up. Last Sunday I did a full turn without putting a hand down.

qa.q: Who suggested putting a star on the calendar?
How did the row of stars make Alka feel when feeling like quitting?
qa.a: Alka felt encouraged, because the row was proof of a lot of showing up even when progress felt slow.

qa.q: What could Alka add to the chart to see skill as well as effort?
qa.a: Write one thing learned beside each star, because it shows improvement and not just the number of days.

qa.q: How might Coach Kamal see the calendar?
qa.a: As a helpful sign of regular practice, since the coach can see the effort at a glance.

grounding: A learner marks a star for each practice day, and the growing row keeps Alka going through slow weeks.
